原页 81

Stories of the Enlightenment often pair knowledge and vision, in two senses: the privileging of the sense of sight, and the importance of planning. Vision has energized knowledge of the globe by condensing it in a friendly visual icon and normalizing its futurist aspirations. Yet global imagery is contested and tentative. Knowledge that travels today is haunted by the disappointments of past visions. Haunting disturbs our reliance on vision. Double vision gives us a headache, reminding us of our frailty. Authoritative knowledge is forced to shore up its boundaries. “Experts” are those who have trained themselves to see with a singular vision. In contrast, the public is troubled by haunting. Only by excluding the public can knowledge be kept pure.
原页 81

启蒙运动的故事常常把知识与视野（vision）相联系，其中包含两层意思：视觉感官的优先地位，以及规划愿景的重要性。视野把关于全球的知识凝聚成一个易于亲近的视觉符号，并使其面向未来的抱负显得理所当然，从而赋予这种知识以活力。然而，全球意象始终受到争议，尚未定型。今天流传的知识仍被过去愿景落空的幽影萦绕。这些幽影扰乱了我们对视野的依赖。重影让我们头痛，提醒我们自身的脆弱。权威知识被迫巩固其边界。“专家”是那些训练自己以单一视野观看的人。相比之下，公众仍受幽影困扰。只有将公众排除在外，知识才能保持纯净。
原页 81

None of this means that any knowledge is as good as any other. Continued life on earth depends on getting our knowledge into as good a shape as possible. But this can mean paying more rather than less attention to the multiplicity of knowledge claims. Both global knowledge and knowledge that travels around the globe are improved by dialogue across difference. Hauntings sometimes open the way to such dialogue: What visions have we been formed by, yet forgotten? What visions have we let shrivel, fester, or fall away?
原页 81
这并不意味着任何知识都和其他知识一样好。地球上的持续生命取决于把我们的知识塑造得尽可能好。但这可能意味着更多而非更少地关注知识主张的多样性。全球知识以及围绕全球旅行的知识，都通过跨越差异的对话而得到改善。萦绕有时为这种对话开辟道路：我们曾被哪些愿景塑造，却又将其遗忘？我们让哪些愿景枯萎、溃烂或消逝了？
原页 81

1955. On April 18, in the town of Bandung, Indonesia’s first president welcomed delegates from across Asia and Africa to what promised to be a momentous occasion: the Asia~Africa Conference. The theme of the president’s opening remarks (“Let a new Asia and a new Africa be born”) was freedom. Freedom was spreading across the globe.
原页 81
1955年。4月18日，在印尼的万隆镇，印尼首任总统欢迎来自亚洲和非洲的代表，参加一场有望意义重大的盛会：亚非会议。总统开场发言的主题（“让新的亚洲和新的非洲诞生”）是自由。自由正在全球蔓延。

Sisters and Brothers, how terrifically dynamic is our time! I recall that, several years ago, I had occasion to make a public analysis of colonialism, and that I then drew attention to what I called the “lifeline of imperialism.” This line runs from the Straits of Gibraltar, through the Mediterranean, the Suez Canal, the Red Sea, the Indian Ocean, the South China Sea and the Sea of Japan. For most of that enormous distance, the territories on both sides of this lifeline were colonies, the peoples were unfree, their futures mortgaged to an alien system. Along that lifeline, that main artery of imperialism, there was pumped the life-blood of colonialism.
兄弟姐妹们，我们的时代是多么充满活力啊！我记得，几年前，我曾有机会对殖民主义作一次公开分析，当时我提请注意我所谓的“帝国主义的生命线”。这条线从直布罗陀海峡出发，穿过地中海、苏伊士运河、红海、印度洋、南中国海和日本海。在这条漫长距离的大部分地方，生命线两侧的领土都是殖民地，人民不自由，他们的未来被抵押给一个异己的制度。沿着这条生命线，这条帝国主义的主动脉，泵送着殖民主义的生命之血。
原页 82

And today in this hall are gathered together the leaders of those same people. They are no longer the victims of colonialism. They are no longer the tools and playthings of forces they cannot influence. Today, you are representatives of free peoples, peoples [of] a different stature and standing in the world. (Sukarno 1983: 5)
原页 82
而今天，正是这些人民的领袖们聚集在这个大厅里。他们不再是殖民主义的受害者。他们不再是那些自己无力影响的势力的工具和玩物。今天，你们是自由人民的代表，是在世界上具有不同地位与身份的人民。（Sukarno 1983: 5）
原页 82

In 1955, the American Revolution still stood as a beacon of freedom—at least in Indonesia, where U.S. influence had helped the independence struggle. President Sukarno reminded his audience that on April 18, 1776, Paul Revere rode at midnight through the New England countryside warning of the approach of British troops in “the first successful anti-colonial war in history” (1983: 7). Sukarno quoted Longfellow:
校注3
原页 82
1955年，美国革命仍然作为自由的灯塔屹立——至少在印尼如此，美国的影响曾帮助独立斗争。苏加诺总统提醒听众，1776年4月18日，保罗·里维尔午夜骑马穿过新英格兰乡村，警告英军逼近，这是“历史上第一场成功的反殖民战争”（1983: 7）。苏加诺引用了朗费罗：
校注3
原页 82
A cry of defiance, and not of fear,
A voice in the darkness, a knock at the door,
And a word that shall echo for evermore!
原页 82
一声反抗的呼喊，而非恐惧的呼喊，
黑暗中的一个声音，门上的一阵敲击，
以及一句将永远回响的话！
原页 82

Yet the echoing U.S. voice was also known for its menace. The atom bomb had been unleashed, and the escalating Cold War threatened the very existence of the world. As Sukarno explained: “War would not only mean a threat to our independence, it may mean the end of civilization and even of human life. There is a force loose in the world whose [potential] for evil no man truly knows. . . .
[I]t has been made clear that the weapons of ultimate horror will certainly be used.... No task is more urgent that that of preserving peace” (1983: 8).

What can we do? We can do much! We can inject the voice of reason into world affairs. We can mobilize all the spiritual, all the moral, all the political strength of Asia and Africa on the side of peace. Yes, we! We, the peoples of Asia and Africa, 1,400,000,000 strong, far more than half the human population of the world, we can mobilize what I have called the Moral Violence of Nations in favor of peace. We can demonstrate to the minority of the world which lives on the other continents that we, the majority, are for peace, not war, and that whatever strength we have will always be thrown on to the side of peace. (1983: 8).

Thus opened what would become known as the Third World, here imagined as a nonaligned block of emerging nations whose united presence could stop the Cold War. Their unity would define them as a global force. Their freedom would sponsor global peace. Peace and freedom would work together to remake the globe.
原页 82
然而，那回响的美国声音也以其威胁而闻名。原子弹已被释放，不断升级的冷战威胁着世界的存在本身。正如苏加诺所解释的：“战争不仅意味着对我们独立的威胁，还可能意味着文明的终结，甚至人类生命的终结。世界上有一种力量在游荡，无人真正知道它的邪恶[潜力]……
已经清楚，终极恐怖的武器一定会被使用……没有比维护和平更紧迫的任务”（1983: 8）。
我们能做什么？我们能做很多！我们可以把理性的声音注入世界事务。我们可以动员亚洲和非洲一切精神的、道德的、政治的力量站在和平一边。是的，我们！我们，亚洲和非洲的人民，14亿之众，远远超过世界人口的一半，我们可以动员我所谓的各国的道德暴力来支持和平。我们可以向生活在其他大陆的少数人证明，我们这些多数人支持和平，而不是战争，我们拥有的一切力量将永远投向和平一边。（1983: 8）
第三世界由此开场，在这里被想象为一个由新兴国家组成的不结盟集团，其团结的存在可以阻止冷战。它们的团结将使它们成为一股全球力量。它们的自由将促进全球和平。和平与自由将共同重塑地球。
原页 83

The guest list at Bandung was a roll call of the celebrities of post-World War II nationalism. Besides Indonesia’s leaders, the sponsors were India’s Jawaharlal Nehru, Burma’s U Nu, Pakistan’s Mohammed Ali, and Ceylon’s Sir John Kotelawala. Gamal Abdel Nasser represented Egypt; Chou En-lai represented China; Prince Sihanouk represented Cambodia; Kwame Nkrumah sent his deputy from the Gold Coast. Ministers from Afghanistan, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Saudi Arabia, Sudan, Syria, Turkey, and Yemen came from the Middle East. Leaders still working for independence came from sub-Saharan Africa. Two delegations represented Vietnam, North and South. In a gesture of solidarity, novelist Richard Wright and U.S. Congressman Adam Clayton Powell came as “unofficial delegates” representing African Americans. Racism was an important conference topic. As Sukarno put it, “This is the first intercontinental conference of colored peoples in the history of mankind” (1983: 3).
原页 83

万隆的宾客名单是二战后民族主义名人的点名。除了印尼领导人，发起者还有印度的贾瓦哈拉尔·尼赫鲁、缅甸的吴努、巴基斯坦的穆罕默德·阿里和锡兰的约翰·科特拉瓦拉爵士。贾迈勒·阿卜杜勒·纳赛尔代表埃及；周恩来代表中国；西哈努克亲王代表柬埔寨；夸梅·恩克鲁玛从黄金海岸派来了副手。来自中东的有阿富汗、伊朗、伊拉克、约旦、黎巴嫩、利比亚、沙特阿拉伯、苏丹、叙利亚、土耳其和也门的部长们。仍在为独立而战的领导人来自撒哈拉以南非洲。两个代表团代表越南，南北各一。作为团结的姿态，小说家理查德·赖特和美国国会议员亚当·克莱顿·鲍威尔作为代表非裔美国人的“非官方代表”前来。种族主义是会议的重要议题。正如苏加诺所说，“这是人类历史上第一次有色人种的洲际会议”（1983: 3）。
原页 83

In Bandung, national sovereignty seemed full of promise. Colonialism was on its way out; freedom was sweeping the globe. Unity among the emerging nations could be a new source of political power, thwarting racism and nuclear war. Solidarity could make peace possible, and peace could guarantee freedom. How many times the world has turned since then! How few today remember the meeting in Bandung.
原页 83
在万隆，国家主权似乎充满希望。殖民主义正在退场；自由正席卷全球。新兴国家之间的团结可以成为政治权力的新来源，挫败种族主义和核战争。团结可以使和平成为可能，和平可以保证自由。从那以后，世界转了多少圈！今天还有多少人记得万隆会议。

In April 2000, I visited the Museum of the Asia-Africa Conference in Bandung with an international group of scholars. The museum itself is a New Order creation, inaugurated in 1980. It trains our eyes with a “conference hall in miniature” exhibit, reducing the conference’s success to its pomp and discipline. It is careful to excise President Sukarno, who was deposed by the New Order, from too much praise. Yet the mythic world of post-World War II nationalism rushes upon us as soon as we see the black-and-white photographs of the delegates. Nasser, Nehru, U Nu: the names themselves resound with the promise of post-colonial development, ‘Third World nations on the move. How young they look—as beautiful as movie stars—how full of optimism and hope! How possible it still seemed that the nations over which these young men had come to preside would overcome colonial legacies to build new worlds of freedom and opportunity. For a moment we can taste the promise that the clasped hands of rising Third World leaders offered. A map of the world, covered with radiating lines, fills one wall: the connections among developing nations will cover the earth.

2000年4月，我和一个国际学者团体参观了万隆的亚非会议博物馆。博物馆本身是新秩序的产物，于1980年落成。它用“微型会议厅”展品训练我们的眼睛，把会议的成功简化为其盛况和纪律。它小心翼翼地避免过多赞扬被新秩序废黜的苏加诺总统。然而，一看到代表们的黑白照片，二战后民族主义的神话世界便扑面而来。纳赛尔、尼赫鲁、吴努：这些名字本身就回响着后殖民发展的承诺，行进中的第三世界国家。他们看起来多么年轻——像电影明星一样美丽——多么充满乐观与希望！这些年轻人已经开始领导的国家，似乎仍很有可能克服殖民遗产，建设自由与机会的新世界。有那么一刻，我们能尝到崛起的第三世界领导人紧握双手所提供的那种承诺。一面墙上挂满一张展开辐射线的世界地图：发展中国家之间的联系将覆盖地球。
原页 84

Meanwhile, we peer at dusty typewriters and telex machines in glass cases: these are the machines that ran the conference. How old and obsolete they seem. This dream of a rising Third World has not lasted. Instead of unity blocking the Cold War, the Cold War blocked the unity of nonaligned nations. Radical nationalists were deposed and murdered; the Cold War was exported to countries across the world. Militaries and development budgets took over. Nationalism lost its promise, as imperially mandated authoritar- ‘an rule came to define the Third World. As the future has shifted, the past contorts, confused. In one cabinet featuring conference pamphlets, the curators have included an engineering report on an airplane crash in another city. No explanation is offered.
原页 84

与此同时，我们凝视玻璃柜里满是灰尘的打字机和电传机：这些是运转会议的机器。它们看起来多么古老、多么过时。这个崛起的第三世界的梦想没有持续。团结没有阻止冷战，冷战反而阻止了不结盟国家的团结。激进的民族主义者被废黜和谋杀；冷战被出口到世界各国。军队和发展预算接管了。民族主义失去了它的承诺，帝国强加的威权统治逐渐定义了第三世界。随着未来的移动，过去扭曲、混乱。在一个陈列会议小册子的柜子里，策展人放入了一份关于另一座城市飞机失事的工程报告。没有任何解释。
原页 84
This past is ours, but through a glass, mythical, and dusty.
原页 84
这个过去是我们的，但隔着玻璃，神话般的，满是灰尘。
原页 84

In 1955, the Bandung conference was commemorated on an Indonesian postage stamp, an enlarged version of which adorns the museum wall. On the lower right side, Asians and Africans raise their hands to release scores of doves. The doves are flying to a great, round, moonlike rising globe, which forms the focus of attention of the crowd. This globe is the earth, illustrated with its Asian and African countries in prominent view.
原页 84
1955年，万隆会议被印在印尼邮票上，其放大版装饰着博物馆墙壁。在右下角，亚洲人和非洲人举起双手，放出数十只鸽子。鸽子飞向一个巨大、圆形、月亮般升起的地球，地球成为人群关注的焦点。这个球体就是地球，其中的亚洲和非洲国家处于显著位置。
原页 84

This is not the globe whose image we naturalize in the twenty-first century. The space shots of the fragile blue-green orb, wrapped in clouds, had not yet been produced. This is still a globe of international maps. Most strikingly, the people are not standing on it. They face it with admiration and hope; they send doves to it. It shines on them, offering them light, but it does not appear to trap them in its vulnerabilities and disciplines.
原页 84
这不是我们在21世纪习以为常的地球形象。那些呈现云层包裹着脆弱蓝绿色球体的太空照片尚未问世。这仍然是一张国际地图的地球。最引人注目的是，人们并不站在它上面。他们带着钦佩和希望面对它；他们把鸽子送向它。它照耀他们，给他们光，但似乎并没有把他们困在它的脆弱与规训中。

In Bandung, the globe was a symbol of what might be possible: national sovereignty and world peace. This global dream space was made possible by other mid-twentieth century uses of the globe, for example in the United Nations. The bridge to this dream space was that of universal truths, such as science, modernization, and political freedom. This was a time when science seemed more than a neutral set of truths. Science was the antidote to ignorant racial stereotypes and misguided imperial impositions. International cooperation among scientists formed a model for coexistence and respect. Similarly, modernization and development might allow each nation to fulfill its dreams while entering cooperative arrangements with others. Human rights might form a peace-loving common language. The doves set off in the Bandung commemorative stamp are universal truths, which forge a bridge to the dream space of global peace and freedom.

在万隆，地球是可能之物的象征：国家主权与世界和平。这个全球梦想空间之所以可能，是因为20世纪中叶地球的其他用途，例如在联合国。通往这个梦想空间的桥梁是普遍真理，如科学、现代化和政治自由。这是一个科学似乎不仅仅是中立真理集合的时代。科学是对无知种族刻板印象和错误帝国强加的解药。科学家之间的国际合作形成了共存与尊重的典范。同样，现代化和发展可能让每个国家在实现梦想的同时，与他国进入合作安排。人权可能形成一种爱好和平的共同语言。万隆纪念邮票上放出的鸽子是普遍真理，它们架起通往全球和平与自由梦想空间的桥梁。
原页 85
When we consider the importance of the Bandung dream of peace and freedom, the inadequacy of the bridge seems hardly a good enough reason to have abandoned the quest.
原页 85
当我们考虑万隆和平与自由梦想的重要性时，这座桥梁的不足似乎不足以成为放弃追求的理由。
原页 85

The universal bridge to a global dream space still beckons to us. The bridge might take us out of our imagined isolation into a space of unity and transcendence: the whole world. We find ourselves like a man looking out from his parochial island toward the vast but hazy world of the mainland. The bridge of universal truths promises to take us there. Yet we walk across that bridge, and we find ourselves, not everywhere, but somewhere in particular. Even if our bridge aims toward the most lofty universal truths—the insights of science, the freedom of individual rights, the possibility of wealth for all—we find ourselves hemmed in by the specificity of rules and practices, with their petty prejudices, unreasonable hierarchies, and cruel exclusions. We must make do, enmeshing our desires in the compromise of practical action. We become hardened, or, alternatively, we are overcome with grief and anger. The bridge we stepped off is not the bridge we stepped upon. Yet to cast away the memory of the first bridge denies desire. ‘To pretend it is the same as the second bridge is the baldest lie of power. It is only in maintaining the friction between the two subjectively experienced bridges, the friction between aspiration and practical achievement, that a critical analysis of global connection is possible.
原页 85

通往全球梦想空间的普遍桥梁仍在召唤我们。这座桥可能带我们走出想象的孤立，进入团结与超越的空间：整个世界。我们发现自己像一个从狭隘岛屿望向辽阔却朦胧的大陆世界的人。普遍真理之桥承诺带我们到那里。然而我们走过那座桥，却发现自己并非无处不在，而是在某个特定的地方。即使我们的桥指向最崇高的普遍真理——科学的洞见、个人权利的自由、所有人致富的可能性——我们仍被规则与实践的特殊性所围困，连同它们的小气偏见、不合理的等级制度和残酷的排斥。我们必须将就，把我们的欲望缠入实际行动的妥协。我们变得强硬，或者反过来，被悲伤和愤怒压倒。我们走下的桥不是我们走上的桥。然而，抛弃第一座桥的记忆就是否认欲望。假装它与第二座桥相同，是权力最赤裸的谎言。只有保持两座主观体验之桥之间的摩擦，即抱负与实际成就之间的摩擦，对全球联结的批判性分析才有可能。
原页 85

Science, modernization, and freedom were simultaneously dream bridges for the development of Third World nations and real-life programs within the contingencies of Cold War politics, elite power grabs, authoritarian regimes, religious wars, ecological disasters, and bureaucracies of expertise. Their ability to mobilize national support and their failure to deliver on their promises are intermeshed in these histories.
原页 85
科学、现代化和自由既是第三世界国家发展的梦想桥梁，也是冷战政治、精英夺权、威权政权、宗教战争、生态灾难和专家官僚制等偶然性中的现实生活纲领。它们动员国家支持的能力与未能兑现承诺，在这些历史中相互交织。

Since the mid-twentieth century, the global dream space has been kicked around like a football claimed first by one team and then another. Environmentalists have wanted it badly, but so have human rights activists, religious sects, and marketers. In the 1990s, corporate public relations took hold of the image of the globe and carried it away. “Globalization” came to mean corporate consolidation, the standardization of world markets, and the deference of national governments to transnational business demands. This global dream space also required a bridge of universal truths, involving neoliberal economic principles and the standardization of property law. Yet even the urgent stridency with which such standards were imposed could not keep other versions of truth from having their say. By the turn of the century, “antiglobalization” politics had begun to gel. The confrontation between demonstrators and police guarding the deliberations of the World Trade Organization in Seattle in 1999 opened a new era of globe-making politics.
The motley demonstrators—like the national representatives at Bandung—hoped that the force of their unity might form a block against dangerous giants.

自20世纪中叶以来，全球梦想空间像足球一样被踢来踢去，先被一支球队宣称，然后被另一支。环保主义者非常想要它，但人权活动家、宗教派别和营销人员也是如此。20世纪90年代，企业公共关系抓住了地球形象并将其带走。“全球化”逐渐意味着企业整合、世界市场的标准化，以及各国政府对跨国商业要求的服从。这个全球梦想空间也需要一座普遍真理的桥梁，涉及新自由主义经济原则和财产法的标准化。然而，即使这些标准被强加时的紧迫尖锐，也无法阻止其他版本的真理发声。到世纪之交，“反全球化”政治开始成形。1999年，示威者与守卫世界贸易组织西雅图会议的警察之间的对抗，开启了一个全球制造政治的新时代。
形形色色的示威者——像万隆的国家代表一样——希望他们团结的力量可以形成一个阻挡危险巨人的集团。
原页 86

Seattle and Bandung could not be more different. Anarchists and children dressed as turtles in the street, versus negotiating heads of state. Police fomenting riot versus police on display. The refusal of the hegemony of nation-states, versus the proud assertion of nation-state autonomy. The critique of development, versus the endorsement of rights to develop. In Seattle, official representatives of Third World nations were notorious for refusing to discuss labor standards: Too many accepted that their power as nations now rested on their ability to offer the cheapest labor and the worst working conditions.
原页 86
西雅图和万隆再不同不过了。一边是街上的无政府主义者和装扮成乌龟的儿童，另一边是参加谈判的国家元首；一边是煽动骚乱的警察，另一边是列队展示的警察；一边拒绝民族国家的霸权，另一边自豪地主张民族国家的自主；一边批判发展，另一边肯定发展权。在西雅图，第三世界国家的官方代表以拒绝讨论劳工标准而臭名昭著：太多人接受，他们作为国家的权力如今取决于提供最廉价劳动力和最恶劣工作条件的能力。
原页 86

Yet both Bandung and Seattle were sites for reclaiming the dream space of the globe. Both offered a bridge of doves to make the dream of a livable globe real. The globe, however, was not the same. In Seattle, the globe could not be projected as a sphere of hope. No one would argue that the world’s problems were caused by a lack of global unity. Instead, demonstrators argued that corporate giants had seized the globe; it was up to transnational activists to take it back. The globe could not be imagined rising hopefully like the full moon; it presented itself as already divided between the discipline of military and machines, on the one hand, and the hopes of resistors, on the other.
原页 86
然而，万隆和西雅图都是夺回全球梦想空间的场所。两者都提供了一座鸽子的桥梁，使可居住地球的梦想成真。然而，这个地球并不相同。在西雅图，地球无法被投射为希望的球体。没有人会论证说，世界的问题源于缺乏全球统一。相反，示威者论证说，企业巨头攫取了地球；跨国活动家有责任把它夺回来。地球无法像满月一样充满希望地升起；它已经呈现为分裂的：一边是军事和机器的纪律，另一边是抵抗者的希望。
原页 86

The universal truths that might form a bridge to global dreams were also contested in Seattle. The momentary unity among labor activists, environmentalists, anarchists, and anti-imperialists did not disguise the lack of common principles that guided their critical assaults. Is the destruction of property a progressive or a destructive strategy? Is the problem for labor refractory countries such as China, or power-hungry ones such as the United States? Would environmental management be improved or worsened by placing its concerns integrally inside free trade? Is Christian prayer a good basis for cosmopolitan solidarity? Each position can be argued with a universal truth, but with different results.
原页 86

可能构成通往全球梦想之桥的普遍真理，在西雅图也受到争夺。劳工活动家、环保主义者、无政府主义者和反帝国主义者之间短暂的团结，并未掩盖指导他们批判性攻击的共同原则的缺失。毁坏财产是进步策略还是破坏策略？对劳工而言，问题在于中国等难以驾驭的国家，还是美国等渴求权力的国家？把环境关切整体置于自由贸易内部，会改善还是恶化环境管理？基督教祈祷是世界主义团结的良好基础吗？每一种立场都可以用普遍真理来论证，但结果不同。

These disagreements are not a reason to give up on anti-globalization politics; they are what make it lively. However, they require a new kind of attention to universal truths, our bridges to global dreams. The principles of justice are multiple and contested: Those who feel the effects of injustice continually stretch the categories through which justice is understood. The play among multiple, contested universals can be described as one kind of friction. Knowledge of the globe, and globally traveling knowledge, depend on this friction.
这类分歧不是放弃反全球化政治的理由；它们正是使这种政治活跃的原因。然而，它们要求对普遍真理——我们通往全球梦想的桥梁——给予一种新的关注。正义原则是多元且受争夺的：感受到不义后果的人不断延伸理解正义的范畴。多种彼此争议的普遍性之间的相互作用，可以被描述为一种摩擦。关于地球的知识，以及在各地旅行的知识，都依赖于这种摩擦。
